description: 30 synthetic support tickets across refunds, account issues, technical, edge cases. Each item ships rubric notes the judge uses to score 1-5 on tone, accuracy, completeness.
prompt_template:
You are a customer support agent for Nimbus, a cloud file storage service ($9/mo Personal, $20/mo Pro, $50/mo Team). The user has written in. Reply directly to them. Be helpful, accurate, warm, and concise (under 180 words). Do NOT invent policies that weren't given to you; if you don't know, say you'll check with the team.

--- KNOWN POLICIES ---
- Refunds: full refund within 14 days of charge, no questions asked. Pro-rated refunds for annual plans cancelled mid-term.
- Storage limits: Personal 100GB, Pro 1TB, Team 5TB per seat.
- Account recovery: requires email verification + last 4 of payment method.
- Data export: available on all plans, ZIP download.
- Sharing: Pro and Team only.
- Outage SLA: Team plan gets credit for outages > 1 hour.

--- USER MESSAGE ---
{message}

items.rubric: Should: confirm 14-day window applies, ask for charge date, offer to process. Should NOT: refuse, gate on reason.
items.message: I signed up for Pro yesterday and realized I don't need it. Can I get my money back?

items.rubric: Charge was 30 days ago, outside 14-day window. Should empathize, explain policy, offer alternative (downgrade, credit, escalation). Should NOT: lie that they qualify.
items.message: I want a refund. I haven't used the service much. I signed up 30 days ago.

items.rubric: Should: explain verification steps (email + last 4 of payment method). Should NOT: reveal account info before verification.
items.message: I can't log in to my account. I forgot my password and the reset email isn't coming through.

items.rubric: Should: ask clarifying questions (file type, size, browser, error message). Should NOT: blindly blame user.
items.message: I keep getting an error when I try to upload. It just says 'upload failed.' I've tried 4 times.

items.rubric: Should: explain Pro -> Team upgrade math, mention pro-rated charge. Should NOT: quote prices not in policy doc.
items.message: We're a 4-person team currently on individual Pro plans. What does it look like to consolidate to Team?

items.rubric: Sharing is Pro/Team only. Should: clearly state Personal doesn't have it, suggest upgrade if needed. Should NOT: invent workarounds.
items.message: How do I share a folder with my mom? She has her own Nimbus account too.

items.rubric: Personal = 100GB. Should: state limit, offer upgrade options. Should NOT: invent custom limits.
items.message: I'm on Personal and almost full. How much storage do I get and what are my options?

items.rubric: User is heated. Should: acknowledge frustration without grovelling, focus on fix. Should NOT: be defensive, lecture, or be sycophantic.
items.message: This is the THIRD time my files have failed to sync. I'm paying $20/mo for this. Fix it or I'm out.

items.rubric: Personal plan, no SLA credit. Should: empathize, explain SLA applies only to Team plan, not promise credit. Should NOT: invent compensation.
items.message: Your service was down for 3 hours yesterday afternoon. I'm on Personal. Do I get any kind of credit?

items.rubric: Team plan + >1 hour = qualifies. Should: confirm credit will be applied, ask for account email.
items.message: We're on Team and the outage yesterday lasted 90 minutes. Are we eligible for credit per the SLA?

items.rubric: Available on all plans, ZIP download. Should: explain how, set expectation on time for large accounts.
items.message: I want to move off Nimbus. How do I get all my files out?

items.rubric: Sensitive. Should: take seriously, ask for account email, recommend password change + 2FA, escalate. Should NOT: be casual.
items.message: I think someone got into my account. There are files I don't recognize.

items.rubric: Should: thank, log it, set realistic expectation (no promise). Should NOT: commit to a roadmap.
items.message: Will you ever add a Linux client? The web app is fine but a native app would be huge.

items.rubric: Should: stay neutral, focus on what Nimbus offers, not bash competitors.
items.message: How is Nimbus different from Dropbox? Trying to decide which to use.

items.rubric: Policy is silent on this. Should: say 'let me check with the team' rather than invent. Should NOT: make up an answer.
items.message: Do you have a HIPAA-compliant tier? We're a small clinic.

items.rubric: Should: explain downgrade process, warn about storage limits if currently over.
items.message: I want to downgrade from Pro to Personal. I'm using about 80GB right now.

items.rubric: Should: ask which card, offer to retry, mention how to update payment method.
items.message: My card was charged twice this month. Can you look into this?

items.rubric: Pro/Team feature. Sharing is plan-gated. Should: confirm sender's plan, walk through how shares work.
items.message: My colleague shared a folder with me but I can't see it. We're both on Pro.

items.rubric: Should: ask platform/version, offer basic troubleshooting (sign out / reinstall / update). Should NOT: blame Apple/Google.
items.message: The iOS app keeps crashing when I open large folders. iPhone 14, latest iOS.

items.rubric: Should: take seriously, ask for the shared link, route to trust & safety. Should NOT: dismiss.
items.message: Someone shared a Nimbus link with me containing what looks like copyrighted material. How do I report it?

items.rubric: Should: educate (what 2FA does, how to enable). Friendly tone.
items.message: What's 2FA and should I turn it on?

items.rubric: Pro-rated refunds for annual plans cancelled mid-term. Should: confirm policy applies, explain math.
items.message: I bought the annual plan 4 months ago. If I cancel now do I get the rest back?

items.rubric: Should: explain admin steps (typically: admin invites via team settings). Set up expectation. Should NOT: invent UI paths not in policy.
items.message: I'm the Team plan admin. How do I add a new seat for my new hire?

items.rubric: Should: respect right to deletion, explain process, set timeline expectation.
items.message: I want to delete my account and all my data. I'm in the EU.

items.rubric: User confused about what plan they're on. Should: ask for email to check, walk through self-serve view.
items.message: Am I on Pro or Team? I forgot which I signed up for.

items.rubric: Asks about two things (sharing + storage). Should: address both, not just one.
items.message: Two questions: can I share a folder with someone who doesn't have Nimbus, and what happens if my shared folder exceeds my plan's storage?

items.rubric: User wrote a wall of text. Should: identify the actual ask, respond to it, not the noise.
items.message: Hi, I've been a customer for years and generally love your product, though there have been ups and downs. Anyway, I have a friend coming to visit next week and we were talking about cloud storage at dinner and he mentioned he uses some other service that lets you share folders read-only. I was wondering, does Nimbus let me share a folder so the other person can view but not edit? Thanks!

items.rubric: User is rude but has a real question buried. Should: address the question politely, not engage with the tone.
items.message: your sync is garbage and your support takes forever. anyway can files I delete be restored?

items.rubric: User writes in casual/abbreviated English. Should: match a reasonable level, stay clear.
items.message: yo how do i kick someone off my team plan they left the company

items.rubric: Should: acknowledge concern, offer to investigate, ask for charge date/amount, not promise refund before checking.
items.message: I see a charge on my card I don't recognize from Nimbus. I don't remember signing up. Can you check?
